why: Reads the effective value for a control that EDITS the stored preference -- one of only two lines in this function that read the store rather than `effective`, which is what makes it the tempting edit. On a device without vibration the switch then shows forced-off, which reads as the preference having been erased: what issue #320 forbids. This was the code until #324, harmless only because the block ran on session-less pages where `loop.ts` corrected it; making the page the sole writer would have shipped it everywhere.
